mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility over the past four weeks signals persistent remote work adoption. This structural shift reduces weekday commuting-adjacent retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks as the baseline of office-anchored consumption remains suppressed.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined from -12.6% to -20.9% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to positive growth for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility (11.1% in t-0w) combined with declining RETAIL_REC (-20.1%) indicates consumers are substituting in-person retail with home-based activities and online shopping. This behavioral lock-in persists, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks unless RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses sharply.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL elevated at 11.1% while RETAIL_REC at -20.1%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -10% while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10%.

candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -20% for one week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points in the following week.
